title: The Rock and Divine Wisdom
english: Wasting men upon the earth. Even in his super-natural and most high words, it is not possible to provide a meadow for those who are the most irrational.

The discourse concerning sensible things and the letter of the scripture is the meadow in this, but even the more ethical ones will not be able to partake, each of them saying of such things: 'Into the place of clover, there he pitched his tent' (Ps 104:18).
Having once surpassed such a state, being no longer slaves of men but having become men, they will say again, each of them: 'You have prepared a table before me' (Ps 23:5).

The mind rejoices the heart of men; not everyone alone is the one having the generation from the one saying, 'I am the vine, the true vine' (John 15:1), but since all sensible things are named earth because of the material.

From these, it is possible to take a word ascending through some analogy to the intelligible. And the beautiful word is brought forth from the earth by nourishing the endos and the man in secret; and from the bodily narratives of the scripture, the mystical word is brought forth beautifully because of the historical things said of the earth.

And the face of the inner man is appeased and made bright by the oil of the nourishing divine light, which alone dissolves diseases and the pains of the soul, differing from the attributed intellect. For the word of God is like the vine, so also the oil is; for he says, 'as an olive tree flourishing in the grove of God' (Ps 80:8). For his teaching, by a diverse relationship, is both vine and oil and bread.

According to an upward leading: the race of deer is at war against the race of gazelles. They hasten, indeed, to bring them up. Such are certainly the disciples of Christ, being ready to avenge every disobedience. And he also enables the power against the gazelles from the one who has extended authority to them to tread upon the gazelles and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy.

These are not the spiritual deer desiring the springs of the waters, the spiritual ones, which are also called oracles; they wear themselves out upon these oracles. And if souls perfected according to virtue are to leap great leaps, imitating the one leaping upon the oracles and running over the mountains and the valleys because of the sharp-sightedness and...

Insightful. But those souls that have arrived at this state and are weaker, called swine, flee to the rock upon which Jesus founds the church as an unconquerable fortress; and this is the confession of the faith. And in Proverbs it is said, 'And the swine, a people not strong, made their dwellings in rocks' (Prov 30:26). It is nothing wonderful that the rock is spoken of both singularly and plurally, meaning Christ who is simply the rock, and who is also [spoken of as] rocks according to various thoughts.

It is suggested by scripture that 'Rock is a refuge for the hyenas,' as perhaps there is a synonymy between the hyena and the swine. It is not for each one to hear [someone] saying, 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who will harm me?' (Ps 118:6) and 'The Lord is my helper' (Ps 118:7), and 'I will not fear; what can man do to me?' (Ps 118:8). The fact that the 'As' [the simile] here written is a demonstrator not of likeness but of truth, just as also in [the phrase] 'As God is good to Israel,' for he does not say God is like good, but truly good. And in the present [passage] then, that the works of God are magnified, is signified by the 'As' [in] 'As your works have been magnified, O Lord' (Ps 103:24). For everything that comes about in wisdom is great of God. And the wisdom of God in which all things came into being is the Lord; for Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24).

Another says that he speaks only concerning the rational [beings]. For to hope and to have expectation toward God, this is hinted at. And they hope to find this at an opportune time, being freed from every deficiency and disease. For when this is given, they will gather it, hastening so much to receive it, so that it may be fed into a basket. And there will exist for them the kindness that is upon such straightness, as [He is] opening for them the hand of your words and the wisdom.

God, providing eternal glory to his own works, rejoices in all that hopes for him. For just as having made all things very good in the beginning (Gen 1:31), he rejoiced in the inhabited world, and he rejoiced in the sons of men when there was not yet transgression, so He would rejoice at the perfection and restoration of the ancient [order] of his works, not out of the joy of God [being] not impassible (for the divine is impassible) but out of the acceptance of those having perfected perfect virtue.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Manifestation of Christ and the Guidance of God
english: If you wish to handle these things spiritually, consider how, when God looks upon [you] according to 'Look upon me' (Ps 103:6) and 'The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous' (Ps 103:9), the earth does not stand firm but trembles as if darkening, as if the material existence were to be cast away and pass away. But God, touching the evil powers because he sees the called ones in their pride, smokes them out, entering into them with a breath, as if into the punishment by fire.

Sing to the Lord, having the presence of the one existing not in voice but in thoughts; and I will sing also in perfect deeds to God, since I have the presence of the one existing, in which I partake of the one existing before the ages and who said 'I am the Being' (Ex 3:14). And conversing in a way pleasing and acceptable to God, I will say, 'Let my conversation be sweet to him.' For he himself says, having accepted the church, 'Your voice is sweet' (Ps 103:2).

Just as according to the history of Samuel ministering continually in the tent of meeting, he saw the face of God, so also those who continually and without interruption examine the dogmas of truth and having practiced the virtues, seek the face of God, desiring to see him with a pure mind. For the face of God is the exact imprint of the hypostasis, being an icon of the invisible God; therefore also the one seeing it immediately sees God.

As for his mouth, to perceive his word, he has given you instructions and commands judged to be both law-giving and precise. Having said 'slaves of God from Abraham' because of the bringing in of the race from Abraham, and 'the chosen ones from Jacob' because they are his and bear his name, and 'an election from the nations' then received into an inheritance, their own Lord and God, he says that his providential judgment is such toward all men.

The number of a thousand generations is not said according to a multitude, but by the appropriation toward the unit, just as also in 'When the thousands are increasing', and 'What is good to me is the law of your mouth, surpassing thousands of gold and silver' (Ps 118:72). Because you are evil and yourselves are partakers of Christ.

We have become [such] through being made worthy of the appearance of the Son of God; for He is the Christ, the one who also spoke to them, and He himself, the Savior, teaches in the Psalms that Abraham your father rejoiced to see my day (Ps 104:12), and did rejoice. When did he not look up with his eyes and stand before God at the oak of Mamre? For then the Scripture says, 'God appeared to Abraham.' And these things, even if they are few, were necessary to be announced to the nations by those commanded there to do this.
Regarding Psalm 104:12a, 'brief' instead of 'few.' For the brief lies in respect to magnitude, but the few is arranged in respect to numbers.

Regarding Psalm 104:18-19, they humbled his feet alone, not binding his soul in shackles, but [the soul] having been made free from iron. For they, being surrounded by shackles, bear the affliction, having the soul bowed down by iron. But he endured this not unto all things; for he limits the end of the affliction, saying that he had held it [fast] until the word of God passed through; according to which, having been transferred from the prison, he became a fosterer and nourisher of all, having grasped the word of the Lord, kindling it to boil in the spirit and being filled with the divine light, with which also he is able to give the exhortation saying, 'Do not quench the Spirit' (Ps 104:20).

Regarding Psalm 104:20-21, and Joseph himself did not [follow] this doctrine; therefore, toward the causes, he says, 'Did you not send me here? For you indeed plotted for evil, but God [plotted] for good' (Ps 104:21).

Regarding Psalm 104:26, since not all are able to depart from the harmful ones by themselves and through themselves, God sends to those who are thus weak the ones capable of being guides and leaders of the way that carries toward the good. And the law of God through Moses and the high-priestly word through Aaron are not [the same]; the one forbidding the deeds, the other ministering to God on our behalf and distributing the graces from Him to us; they are the leaders [whom they say], 'Let us flee Egypt.'

Regarding Psalm 104:37, but by upward movement, think how each of those in these guards, possessing health and strength, says, 'I am able to do all things in the one who strengthens me' (Ps 104:37), and enriching in...

title: Repentance and the Divine Mercy
english: It happens through good works, every kind of word, and all knowledge, in silver and gold, and outside of Egypt by God. For it is impossible for one being weak and lacking the aforementioned silver and gold to come out of Egypt.

The set-forth voice is especially holy of those before the coming of the Savior, entreating that the Lord might remember them in the good pleasure of His people (Ps 105:4–6), since He was well-pleased in His beloved Son to save, judging His people and the world; thus he says, showing Him: 'This is my beloved Son in whom I am well-pleased' (Matt 3:17). Because the divine prophets, desiring to see and hear the things happening and being spoken concerning Jesus by the eye of the mind, are worthy that their memory be made in the salvation according to the good pleasure.

And Christ is often called the salvation of God, as also in Ezekiel: 'For all flesh is the salvation of our God' (Ezek 36:26). This visitation, the father of the baptizer making manifest concerning God, says: 'Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in whom he visited us, the sunrise from on high' (Luke 1:78). Having visited us in His salvation, it will be for us to become His chosen ones and to behold in the goodness of His chosen ones the joy being fulfilled, and to be made glad in the divine feast of the nation being completed from all those believing.

And may it be accomplished for us also to be praised with His inheritance, for it is for us as heirs to have the inheritance. Who is this church from the Gentiles, saying, 'Let them depart from me, and I will give you the inheritance of the Gentiles' (Isa 66:8)? For spiritually, remaining according to the Gospel, those attending to the law are praised with the aforementioned inheritance. And they are praised by God and by the holy powers, receiving those who hasten to be well-pleasing to God.

And the divine men, taking up also the countenance of those who repent of those on whom they acted wickedly, and teaching how they must repent after the sins, saying, 'We have not sinned, but we have sinned like our fathers'—calling their fathers the ancestors and those who came before, or those who begat them in wickedness—will not say everything when confessing, saying, 'We have turned away'...

We have acted perversely and done wrong. And even regarding those who are counted among those who repent, they do not appear to have been pious. For we were not made outside of the divinity, but being contained by it, we were defeated by passions and hard toil, and we sinned and did other things. Psalm 105:9: God, who rebuked the Red Sea, is praised by all. If even Jesus, when the sea is tossing, rebukes the sea, so that from a storm a calm becomes, He is proven to be God, He who rebuked the Red Sea, and He is the Son of Him. But because God rebuked the Red Sea, the ancient sea becomes dry, as if it were to be passable, and the abyss is no longer called by the abundance of the waters. Psalm 105:19: And they made a calf in Horeb, having a vision of the Apis brought from Egypt in Memphis. Therefore, they worshiped this calf and other carvings, being bound to the drama of polytheism. Immediately, indeed, having made a calf, they were showing many, saying, 'These are not your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'

The following psalm, its praise being of the divine benefits and mercies toward men that have been done, has the sequence arranged. Psalm 106:1: Those upon whom the surrounding tribulations fall (without any of them bringing this upon themselves), knowing that the good God has these things, says the following verses. And since some are becoming in temporary things thought to be good, they do not simply have a trial of God's mercy, but are being pitied for ever, having the eternal good things from Him. For if even the good God has pitied someone with eternal mercy. He also makes mercy for thousands for those who love Him the same, preparing for them. An eye has not seen, nor has an ear heard, nor has it ascended to the heart of man. It is said also previously that the good is synonymous with the good. Psalm 106:4: Therefore also, being in the desert, we wandered, not having a guide and a leader to follow, finding either a city well-arranged after the holy law in which we were able to dwell without departing from it, but virtue and the wisdom of God.
